text:
lucas: Quick heads-up — I sketched a short roadmap for telemetry granularity across staging. Want to align before we lock any schema changes. TL;DR: trim some envelope fields in staging to cut ingest cost, keep enough attrs for trace reassembly and billing.
anya: please paste the sketch or gist?
mike: +1 to seeing the details. we should avoid any change that blocks replay or late-enrich workflows.
lucas: gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/telemetry-granularity-draft (contains table and sample payloads). main proposal: drop 'debug_meta' and per-span 'full_backtrace' in staging streams, sample 1% raw traces to a raw-store for replays, and canonicalize billing_key resolution to header-first then attribute fallback.
trina: concerns: if we drop debug_meta, do we risk missing root-cause context during incident replay? maybe keep it for error spans only? :thinking_face:
mike: error-only retention sounds reasonable. also we should keep a compact fingerprint for query correlation (sha256 of important attrs) to avoid storing the whole payload.
omar (sre-bot): deploy-bot: Created a test branch and a staging canary: telemetry/granularity/refactor. CI: 2/3 checks passed.
anya: costs: what's the expected ingest delta? I need a ballpark for finance.
lucas: quick estimate: 22% ingest volume reduction on staging traces, ~9% overall telemetry cost reduction because metrics/logs unchanged. numbers from a sample week of high-traffic endpoints.
trina: tradeoffs: query surface will change — some ad-hoc debug queries will need enrichment to fetch trimmed fields. we should add a helper API for late-enrich during on-call.
mike: agree. we can add a small service (late-enrich-proxy) that fetches from raw-store by trace-fingerprint and rehydrates. that keeps normal queries fast.
anya: rollout plan idea: 1) wire up sampling and fingerprinting in collector 2) start 1% raw sample -> raw-store 3) begin dropping heavy fields in staging and run dashboards for 2 weeks 4) gradually increase sample or adjust rules, then decide on prod.
lucas: I'd add a step: automated alert on missing billing_key resolution rates >0.5% — we don't want blackholes in cost attribution.
omar (sre-bot): alert rule created: /alerts/telemetry/billingkey-resolution-rate with threshold 0.5% on staging.
trina: schema question: how do we version this change? consumers will need to know when 'debug_meta' may be absent. semantic version header? or use envelope.version attr?
mike: use envelope.schema_version string (major.minor). collectors emit v1.13 for this change. consumers check at decode time and fallback gracefully. document in the catalog.
anya: docs + migration checklist needed. I'll own the consumer compatibility doc.
lucas: OK. pending items: - finalize sample retention TTL for raw-store (propose 30 days) - proto for fingerprint field (sha256 hex, 64 chars) - update collector config: sampling rules and drop list - create migration PR for console dashboards to fallback on enrichment API.
mike: I can take the collector config PR and the fingerprint proto.
trina: I'll spec the rehydrate API and runbook for on-call.
anya: I'll draft the consumer compat doc + cost delta writeup for finance.
omar (sre-bot): note: scheduled a follow-up sync in #eng-platform for Tue 10am.
lucas: thanks all. quick question: does anyone object to 30d raw retention for staging?
anya: I think 30d is fine for staging; for prod we may want 7d by default with ability to extend per-customer.
mike: +1. keep prod conservative by default.
trina: fine. can we add opt-in retention flag per-tenant?
lucas: yes — add tenant_override retention field in dedicated configs. put it in the RFC.
anya: will do.
mike: I'll open the collector PR today, reference the gist and link this thread.
lucas: perfect. if no blockers, I'll mark the sketch as approved and we can start the canary tomorrow. :rocket:
